dedupe_keys.name: framework for global river flood risk assessment winsemius et al 2013 pcr globwb dynrout and 1 km downscaling

description: This 2013 article in Hydrology and Earth System Sciences proposes a framework for strategic global assessments of river flood risk in current and future conditions. Hazard is estimated at about 1 km2 from global climate forcing, a global hydrological model, a global flood routing model and an inundation downscaling routine; the second component combines hazard with impact models at the same resolution for damage, affected GDP and affected population, giving indicators such as annual expected damage. The authors applied it with the PCR-GLOBWB model and its optional DynRout flood routing, with scenarios from the IMAGE integrated assessment model, and demonstrated the downscaling and risk estimate in Bangladesh. Coverage is global in design, with Bangladesh as the first case study. Access is free as an open access paper under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the article page gives no code or data download, so reuse needs the underlying models, and the name GLOFRIS is not used on the abstract page. Simulation uses: flood hazard and risk scenarios for infrastructure exposure under climate and socio-economic change. Related records: FLOPROS (data-flopros-global-flood-protection-standards) and WRI Aqueduct (data-wri-aqueduct-water-risk-atlas).
